items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to requiring state agencies to provide certain information to unsuccessful bidders during the debriefing process
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3450

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to
requiring state agencies to provide certain information to
unsuccessful bidders during the debriefing process

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to require state agencies to provide
information to unsuccessful bidders during the debriefing process
describing why their proposal or bid was not selected, and why the
winning proposal or bid was selected.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph c of subdivision 9 of section 163 of the
state finance law, as amended by chapter 137 of the laws of 2008, to
include debriefing the unsuccessful proposal or bid, why the winning
bid was selected and provide advice or guidance on methods for
improving future bids.

Section 2 provides an immediate effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, state agencies are required to provide a debriefing to any
unsuccessful offerer that responded to a request for proposal or an
invitation for bids, and describe the reasons that the proposal or bid
submitted by the unsuccessful offerer was not selected for award.
However, the state agencies do not currently have to explain why the
winning bid was ultimately selected, or provide advice or guidance on
methods for improving future bids. This bill would allow unsuccessful
offerers the ability to understand why their offer was not selected
and where they need to improve in order to have their bid or proposal
awarded. This bill would benefit all New Yorkers by guarantying that
the best bid or proposal is selected and that those that aren't
selected are able to improve and better compete for awards.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 294

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:

Senate Bill Number 3450-C, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the state finance law, in relation to requiring
      state agencies to  provide  certain  information  to  unsuccessful
      bidders during the debriefing process"

Senate Bill Number 5713-B, entitled:

    "AN  ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to allowing the
      state comptroller to excuse non-material deviations in a  procure-
      ment;  in  relation to participation by state agencies in a system
      used by the comptroller to compile vendor responsibility  informa-
      tion;  in relation to defining information technology for procure-
      ment purposes; in relation to authorizing the commissioner of  the
      office  of general services and state agencies to develop alterna-
      tive procurement methods not otherwise  authorized  by  law  under
      certain  circumstances;  in  relation  to  authorizing competitive
      negotiation concluding with a best and final offer; in relation to
      clarifying the use of best and final offers  for  invitations  for
      bids  and requests for proposals for goods, services and technolo-
      gy; in relation to providing unsuccessful  offerors  a  reasonable
      opportunity  for debriefing; in relation to increasing the thresh-
      old for construction bonds; in relation to clarifying the  use  of
      contracts  let  by  another  governmental  agency;  in relation to
      reports on centralized contracts; and in  relation  to  increasing
      the  threshold  for  the  state  comptroller's approval of certain
      contracts and clarifying the valuation of  non-cash  contracts  by
      the state comptroller"

    NOT APPROVED

  These  bills  would amend various statutory provision of State Finance
Law (SFL) Sections 112, 137, and 163 relating to public  procurement  of
commodities, services, technology, and public works.

  While  the  bills purportedly seek to streamline the state procurement
process and provide unsuccessful bidders with an opportunity to  improve
their  chances of competing for future solicitations, many of the amend-
ments would place unnecessary limitations and restrictions on the abili-
ty  of  state  agencies  to  conduct  public  procurements  while  other
provisions  fail  to  articulate  clear  standards for proposed changes.
Moreover, it is well-established that  input  from  the  affected  state
agencies  has  always  been a critical component of any effort to modify
procurement laws and regulations. In this instance, however, state agen-
cies were not consulted during the drafting and negotiation process.

  Finally, SFL Section 163, which forms the backbone of the law  govern-
ing  the  procurement  of  commodities,  services,  and technology, will
expire on June 30, 2016. Given the substantial fiscal, operational,  and
policy  concerns  that must be addressed, and consistent with past prac-
tice, any substantive changes to SFL Section 163 and related procurement
laws should be made in the course of three-way negotiations  during  the

2016  legislative  session.  For these reasons, I am constrained to veto
this bill.

  However,  in  an  effort  to  facilitate  engagement on this important
issue, I am directing the Office of General Services to initiate roundt-
able discussions, which will include representatives from  the  relevant
state  agencies,  stakeholders,  and  legislative  staff, to discuss the
proposed revisions and identify necessary  changes  to  the  procurement
laws, which will promote the efficiency and effectiveness of the process
and promote greater efficiency and information sharing.

  These bills are disapproved.                (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
